episodes.193318: Scattered strong to severe storms develop during the late afternoon hours on 8/18. The environment featured a gradient in instability with weaker instability across the western Midlands (mixed layer CAPE around 1000 J/kg) to stronger instability across the central and eastern Midlands (mixed layer CAPE around 2000-2500 J/kg) with sufficient effective bulk shear around 30-35 knots. There was a gradient in moisture with Precipitable water values ranging from 1.5 inches to 1.8 inches in the eastern counties. Some drier air aloft was moving into the area with some downsloping winds at 850/700mb as the upper trough axis approached. The best forcing remained to our north over VA/NC.
episodes.193375: A period of northwest flow persisted across Central Alabama for a few days in mid-August, with a ridge over the southwestern United States and an upper low over the Great Lakes. A storm in Cherokee County produced damage on August 16, and storms the next day produced damage across central and eastern counties. On August 18, numerous thunderstorms passed through central and southern counties in Central Alabama, producing widespread tree damage and several instances of hail. A couple areas in Coosa and Tallapoosa counties saw hail up to golf ball size.
episodes.193496: Severe thunderstorm moved through eastern Laramie County into the Nebraska Panhandle the afternoon of 19 August.
episodes.193499: A severe thunderstorm moved from eastern Laramie County Wyoming into Kimball County the afternoon of 19 August.
episodes.193811: A combination of high instability and above average deep layer shear for August with an upper level disturbance resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms. Some storms were severe with damaging wind gusts.
episodes.193812: A combination of high instability and above average deep layer shear for August with an upper level disturbance resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms. Some storms were severe with damaging wind gusts.
episodes.193813: A combination of high instability and above average deep layer shear for August with an upper level disturbance resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms. Some storms remained strong all the way to the coast with measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.194006: Severe thunderstorms developed along a convergence boundary that stretched from Limon to Sterling. The storms produce hail up to an inch and a half in diameter, winds to 60 mph, two landspout tornadoes and flash flooding.
episodes.194113: Pre-frontal and sea breeze induced storms moved offshore of the local Atlantic coast and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.194123: A strong cold front located along Appalachia on the afternoon of the 18th quickly tracked eastwards and moved into the Coastal Plain during the late overnight hours on the 18th to the early morning hours on the 19th. Out ahead of this front shower and thunderstorms developed across the Piedmont during the afternoon on the 18th and eventually tracked east across the Coastal Plain and eventually the waters of Eastern North Carolina during the early morning hours of the 19th with a few of these storms becoming strong to severe in nature. These storms brought damaging wind gusts to our coastal waters and the Pamlico Sound.
episodes.194126: A cold front stalled across the Coastal Plain during the afternoon of August 19th. As this occurred, isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along the Coastal Plain just out ahead of this front and gradually tracked eastwards into the northern coastal waters and Pamlico Sound on the evening of August 19th. A few of these storms brought damaging wind gusts to the waters from Pamlico Sound north.
episodes.194195: Thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall that led to isolated instances of flooding.
episodes.194251: An active week of severe weather unfolded across the Northern Rockies from August 18th through the 21st. Subtle waves lifting through a southwesterly flow aloft just west of an upper level ridge combined with ample surface heating and shear to result in multiple rounds of severe weather, most notably on August 19th when a line of strong thunderstorms lifted northward across the plains and adjacent areas.
episodes.194448: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.194449: Severe thunderstorms produced large hail on August 19.
episodes.194637: A combination of high instability and above average deep layer shear for August with an upper level disturbance resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms. Some storms were severe with damaging wind gusts.
episodes.194794: A thunderstorm became severe in northwest Crook County and tracked east-southeast across the county. The storm produced hail up to baseball size and wind gusts to 80 mph. The Devils Tower area sustained significant damage to trees and property. The storm also became tornadic for a brief period over the Bear Lodge Mountains, south of Alva. Many trees were either uprooted or snapped in half along the path, but no property was impacted by the tornado.
episodes.194809: A strong thunderstorm developed over eastern Custer County, producing up to penny sized hail southeast of Fairburn.
episodes.194810: A strong thunderstorm developed over the eastern slopes of the Black Hills, producing hail to nickel size west of Hermosa.
episodes.195202: A shortwave moved across Wyoming and brought severe thunderstorms to portions of central Wyoming. A 60 mph wind gust was reported at the Lander airport in Fremont County. In Johnson County, quarter size hail was reported to the southeast of Linch.
episodes.195278: Weak forcing in an unstable atmosphere led to a few instances strong winds.
episodes.195279: Weak forcing in an unstable atmosphere led to a few instances of strong winds.
episodes.195280: Weak forcing in an unstable atmosphere led to a few instances of strong winds.
episodes.195324: A pre-frontal trough and an approaching cold front from upstream thunderstorms combined to spark two areas of storm development that produced severe and damaging wind gusts. The most prolific was a microburst in western Johnston County that shut down Interstate 40 for several hours between North Carolina highway 42 and North Carolina highway 210.
episodes.195325: Behind a lead effective front that passed through the day prior, a slow moving cold front moving east of the mountains sparked additional thunderstorm development in a marginal severe environment. The best storm of the day quickly deepened over southeast Guilford County and produced severe winds and quarter inch hail as the storm core collapsed.
episodes.195368: A few widely scattered thunderstorms produced several gale-force wind gusts over the tidal Potomac River and the Chesapeake Bay from midday through mid evening.
episodes.195369: A thunderstorm affected a small portion of the tidal Choptank River with gale-force wind gusts.
episodes.195387: A couple of isolated severe thunderstorms produced very localized wind damage in King George County, Virginia, and in the western suburbs of Baltimore.
episodes.195478: High pressure was over Texas in tandem with northwesterly flow on the east side of the high brought a disturbance through Arkansas leading to severe thunderstorms that tracked from northwest to southeast across the state. At the surface, a cold front boundary provided a lifting mechanism for the thunderstorms as the boundary moved from north to south across the state.
episodes.195525: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed southeast across eastern Nebraska and eastern Kansas during the morning and afternoon of the 18th. These thunderstorms weakened before moving into northwestern Arkansas, but additional thunderstorms developed over northwestern Arkansas along the outflow boundary that pushed out from these decaying thunderstorms. The atmosphere over northwestern Arkansas became very unstable during the late afternoon and early evening, which enable some of these storms to produce large hail up to ping pong ball size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195539: Conditions for organized convection were less favorable on August 19th in comparison to previous days, with plenty of moisture but very limited upper level support or instability. However, the terrain of western Colorado acts as a source of lift, and differential daytime heating between the lower and higher valleys can add a boost of instability to that already present with the abundant monsoonal moisture. It was just this scenario on the afternoon of the 19th that allowed showers and storms to form over the San Juan mountains over Hinsdale county. The abundant moisture combined with slow storm motion to increase the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding, and debris flows across that area.
episodes.195597: Waves of showers and thunderstorms ahead of a cold front produced widespread showers and thunderstorms. A few storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts, knocking down trees and power lines across portions of eastern Pennsylvania.
episodes.195753: A series of storms dropped copious amounts of rainfall across northern Alaska from August 15th through the 23rd.  This rainfall caused rapid rises on streams and rivers which resulted in localized flooding of low-lying areas along northern Interior rivers.
episodes.195762: Strong instability, moderate levels of downdraft CAPE, ample bulk shear and a passing mid-level shortwave led to an environment supportive of strong/severe thunderstorms upstream, before activity entered Southeast Georgia with a cold front during evening hours.
episodes.195763: Strong instability, moderate levels of downdraft CAPE, ample bulk shear and a passing mid-level shortwave led to an environment supportive of strong/severe thunderstorms upstream, before activity approached the coast and entered coastal waters with a cold front during evening hours.
episodes.195764: Strong instability, moderate levels of downdraft CAPE, ample bulk shear and a passing mid-level shortwave led to an environment supportive of strong/severe thunderstorms upstream, before activity entered Southeast South Carolina with a cold front during evening hours.
episodes.195765: Modest instability near a weak front placed along the Southeast Coast led to thunderstorms capable of producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195857: As mid-level troughing deepened over the East Coast U.S., it sent an associated frontal boundary into the Southeast US on August 19th and further into Central Florida on the 20th. With this frontal boundary, it supported showers and thunderstorm over the southeastern Florida metro and adjacent waters. Passing storms brought the threat for strong, gusty winds and waterspouts over the marine areas.
episodes.195868: Isolated thunderstorms moved into the North Carolina Piedmont during the afternoon into the evening. A few of the storms produced strong-to-damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195894: An area of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in 1 inch hail in Tucson and severe threshold wind at the Nogales International Airport.
episodes.195901: A remnant cold pool from an MCS in the Central Mississippi Valley was able to tap into afternoon summertime instability on the evening of the 18th. Thunderstorms were scattered in nature but relatively long lived with stretches of wind damage originating from individual cells all the way from the Atlanta Metro down past Macon.
episodes.195914: Scattered storms developed over Central Louisiana along a cold front. A couple of damage reports were received.
episodes.195971: Thunderstorms moved across southwest Alabama and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.196025: Thunderstorms developed across southeast Mississippi and produced gusty winds.
episodes.196079: An active upper level pattern with a series of shortwave troughs moving over the region throughout the course of the week produced several days of strong to severe thunderstorms over the region.
episodes.196096: Showers and thunderstorms developed off the Wasatch and Uinta Mountains mid-afternoon on Sunday the 18th of August. They crossed into southwest Sweetwater County and brought locally heavy rainfall. At around 6 PM, the river gauge on the Henry���s Fork at Manila began to spike and exceeded Flood Stage by 7:30 PM. The gauge crested near 12.5 feet at around 8:45 PM and quickly dropped back below flood stage by 10 PM. A few reports were gathered from local officials and via social media describing and showing minor flooding just north of Manila UT in the Henry's Fork river drainage. A flood survey was conducted on Aug 26 by NWS RIW and CYS employees. Several locations of agricultural flooding and significant bank erosion upstream of the gauge were noted, but no infrastructure damages were observed or known.
episodes.196102: Had another in a period of severe weather days.

episodes.196116: Thunderstorms brought gusty winds to much of Utah and flash flooding to southern Utah.

episodes.196135: Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of a secondary cold front moving across Virginia on August 19. These storms produced gusty winds as they moved over the Virginia Coastal Waters.
episodes.196191: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms organized along remnant outflows from earlier convection across Central and Southeast Arkansas during the evening hours on August 18th. Observed soundings nearby reflected over 2000 J/kg of MLCAPE and 35 knots of effective shear. Despite some slight nocturnal cooling, the overall organization of the cold pool allowed strong to severe thunderstorms to continue a few hours after sunset. As a result, a few damaging wind reports were recorded across Union Parish Louisiana.
episodes.196196: A frontal system over the area on August 18th produced heavy thunderstorms that were fairly slow moving over northeast New Jersey. A cold front moving in from the west late in the afternoon produced heavy thunderstorms with an environmental MUCAPE of 2000-3000 J/kg and PWAT values of 1.7-1.8 inches. These slow moving thunderstorms produce rainfall rates of 1-3 inches per hour over New Jersey with total rainfall amounts of 2-4 inches. This resulted in widespread flash flooding during the evening of August 18th.
episodes.196197: A frontal system over the area on August 18th and into the early morning hours of August 19th allowed for the development of multiple rounds of slow moving heavy thunderstorms which resulted in widespread significant to catastrophic flash flooding for portions of Southeast New York, specifically for the north shore of Long Island. Several rounds of rain moved through during the day on August 18th. By the afternoon, a line of thunderstorms moving in from the west interacted with several mesoscale boundaries and allowed the thunderstorms to intensify and train over Long Island during the overnight hours into early on August 19th. These thunderstorms produced rainfall rates of upwards of 3-5 inches per hour with total rainfall amounts of upwards of 10 inches, much of it falling over a 2-4 hour period. This resulted in numerous water rescues, several dam breaks, several road washouts, and significant damage to numerous buildings across the north shore of Long Island.
episodes.196217: An upper level trough approached aloft as a cold front approached at the surface. Clusters of showers and thunderstorms developed west of the area. Given 0-6 km Bulk Shear and MLCAPE values around 1000 J/kg, some storms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.196219: An upper level trough approached aloft as a cold front approached at the surface. Clusters of showers and thunderstorms developed west of the area. Given 0-6 km Bulk Shear and MLCAPE values around 1000 J/kg, one storm became severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.196238: An isolated waterspout was observed near No Name Key in association with a reverse convective cloud line.
episodes.196271: A cold front tracked through eastern New York on August 19, 2024, forcing the development of scattered showers and broken lines of thunderstorms. Multiple rounds of heavy downpours impacted northeast Albany County, leading to a few instances of flooding and flash flooding just outside the city of Albany and within the town of Colonie. Flooded roadways led to traffic delays.
